name: Welcome to Terraline 👋
description_html:
Hey there! This demo project is your playground to see how a team runs services in Terraline. Click around, change things, and don't worry about breaking anything.

Each work item walks you through one part of running a service — from setting it up to triaging what comes in. Follow along card by card, or jump straight to what you need.

First thing to try

  1. Find the Properties section below where it says State: Todo.

  2. Click it and change it to Done, or drag this card to the Done column.
description_stripped: This demo project shows how a team runs services in Terraline. Each work item walks you through one part — follow along card by card, or jump straight to what you need.

name: 1. Create a project for your service 🎯
description_html:
A project is where a service lives in Terraline — its work items, requests, runbooks, and the people who run it.

Note: this demo is already set up as a project, and the cards you're reading are work items inside it. Here's how you'd create your own when you're ready.

  1. Open the Projects list from the sidebar and choose Create project.

  2. Give it a name and an identifier — something short your team will recognise in work item IDs.

  3. Add a description so anyone landing here knows which service this is.

Tip: keep one project per service. If two teams run the same service, they can share the project and split work with Modules.

name: 2. Invite your team 🤜🤛
description_html:
Running a service is a team effort. Invite the people who triage, resolve, and own it.

  1. Open workspace Settings → Members and choose Add member.

  2. Invite by email and pick a role: Admin for the people who configure the workspace, Member for day-to-day work, Guest for stakeholders who only need to follow along.

  3. Use project settings when someone should only work in one service.

Roles decide what people can see and change, so start with the least access someone needs.
description_stripped: Invite the people who triage, resolve, and own the service. Pick roles — Admin, Member, Guest — with the least access each person needs.

name: 3. Log requests and incidents ✏️
description_html:
Every piece of work is a work item. A request, an incident, a task, a change — same building block, different properties.

  1. Press C anywhere, or click + New Work Item.

  2. Give it a name, then set Priority, Assignee, and State so it lands in the right queue.

  3. Add labels to group work across services, and attach a runbook page if the fix is already written down.

Work items can be split into sub-work items when a fix has several steps. Use Modules when the work spans more than one cycle.
description_stripped: Every piece of work is a work item: a request, an incident, a task, a change. Name it, set priority, assignee, and state so it lands in the right queue.

name: 4. Visualize your work 🔮
description_html:
The same work items can be viewed in different ways depending on what you need to see.

  • List and Kanban — day-to-day triage and handovers.

  • Calendar — what's due when, and what's coming up.

  • Spreadsheet — bulk edits across many work items.

  • Gantt — dependencies and timelines for larger rollouts.

Save any combination of filters as a View so the whole team opens the same queue. Start with the Urgent requests view already saved in this project.
description_stripped: The same work items can be viewed as a list, kanban, calendar, spreadsheet, or gantt. Save filters as a view so the whole team opens the same queue.

name: 5. Timebox work with cycles 🗓️
description_html:
A Cycle is a timebox: a week, a fortnight, or a maintenance window. Use it to agree what the team takes on and keep progress visible.

  1. Open Cycles and create one for the period you're planning.

  2. Add work items to it — only what the team can realistically finish.

  3. At the end, move unfinished work to the next cycle and start again.

For efforts longer than a cycle — a platform migration, a service onboarding — group work items into a Module instead.
description_stripped: A Cycle is a timebox — a week, a fortnight, or a maintenance window. Add what the team can finish, then roll unfinished work to the next cycle.

name: 6. Customize your settings ⚙️
description_html:
Terraline works the way your team works. A few settings make it fit your service management practice.

  • States — rename them to match your process: Triage, Waiting on customer, Resolved.

  • Labels — add incident, service request, change, or your own categories.

  • Estimates — switch to a system your team already uses.

  • Features — turn Cycles, Modules, Pages, or Intake on and off per project.

You can change all of this later — nothing here is permanent.
description_stripped: States, labels, estimates, and project features make Terraline fit your service management practice. Nothing here is permanent.
